title: Right extension commutes with tower direct image
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite-dimensional field extension of Q_l in universe u, T and S schemes in universe t, and g : T → S. Use the positive-index coefficient sheaves O_E/(l)^(n+1), their specified quotient maps, and the coefficient tower categories and normalized equivalences of det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian. For any recorded abelian tower structures dT,dS and evaluation right adjoints rT,rS, and every n : ℕ, right extension at n followed by tower direct image is naturally isomorphic to finite-level direct image followed by right extension at n: (rT.right n ⋙ dT.equivalence.inverse) ⋙ spTowerPush l E g ≅ spLevelPush l E g n ⋙ (rS.right n ⋙ dS.equivalence.inverse).

source.place: sk-lem-sp-tower-levels-adjoint.proof.md, Well-defined and Adjunction; ordinary operations clause

proof.text: The normalization above n identifies right extension followed by evaluation at n with the identity, using the equivalence counit and restriction along the identity coefficient map. Evaluation commutes with tower direct image. Thus evaluation at n of F = rT,n ⋙ g_* is canonically g_*,n.

The unit of evaluation_n ⊣ rS,n gives F → evaluation_n(F) rS,n, followed by the preceding isomorphism. Its level-n map is invertible: the right-adjoint/evaluation composite is the identity, so the adjunction counit is invertible; the triangle identity makes evaluation of the unit invertible.

Above n the right extensions have identity underlying transition functions, hence bijective transitions. The normalized equivalence transports bijectivity through its counit. Pushforward preserves these transition bijections because it precomposes sections with base change. The compatibility square of the comparison with transitions propagates its level-n bijectivity to every higher level. Below n both sides are zero, and the unique comparison between zero objects is invertible. Sectionwise bijective linear maps are isomorphisms; component inverses assemble into a strict tower inverse. Reflect through the normalized equivalence and obtain the natural tower isomorphism. This also covers n=0 and the zero tower.
